identity.description: WooCommerce: open-source ecommerce plugin for WordPress, maintained by Automattic/WooCommerce.
identity.identity_notes: Sources describe WooCommerce as the open-source ecommerce platform for WordPress; the REST API docs are on woocommerce.com and developer.woocommerce.com. Note the product is a WordPress plugin, not a standalone hosted SaaS, so you need a WordPress site to call its API.

auth.oauth_flows: No OAuth 2.0 flow documented. Over HTTP the docs require OAuth 1.0a 'one-legged' authentication. A separate /wc-auth/v1/authorize endpoint lets an external app request keys with scope read, write, or read_write, returning keys via callback POST.
auth.token_refresh: No refresh tokens; consumer key/secret are long-lived and can be revoked and regenerated in the admin.
auth.scopes_notes: Key permissions are read, write, or read_write, set per key; each key is tied to a WordPress user. MCP remote access uses a WordPress username plus Application Password, with the default server requiring the read capability.

access.production_restrictions: No vendor sandbox was found. Testing needs a WordPress site with WooCommerce installed (free plugin); you create keys yourself as the site admin (manage_woocommerce). Keys for a store you do not administer require that store's admin to issue them. Hosting cost for a WordPress site is not covered by the sources.

write_ops: Batch create/update/delete on coupons and customers
api.limitations: Docs are version-specific (v3 is current); the developer docs name only a few resources in prose, and the full set is in the v3 reference. Rate limits not documented. Webhooks fire on core topics and disable after 5 consecutive failed deliveries. MCP feature is described as a developer preview that may change. Legacy REST API requires a separate plugin for old webhook setups.

open_questions: Rate limits for the REST API are not documented in the sources reviewed.
Whether a vendor sandbox or free hosted test store exists is unknown; testing requires a self-hosted or hosted WordPress site.
Whether the WordPress MCP Adapter-based server counts as 'official' is a judgment call: WooCommerce documents it, but the runtime and the only WooCommerce-org repo (wc-mcp-ability) is a demo.
Full per-resource method lists in the v3 reference were truncated; only coupons, customers, order notes, and order refunds were confirmed.
Trial availability and hosting costs for a test store were not established.
Customers and coupons read/write confirmed; reports and settings write support not confirmed.
Quote verification: many quotes come from fetch-tool extractions, not raw page text; treat as needing re-check against live pages.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented REST interface.
